findings.title: canView(ClientModel) short-circuits on canView(), bypassing client-specific negative permissions
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel client)`, calling `canView()` checks `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` against the all-clients (`"Clients"`) resource before `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` is reached. If an all-clients `view` permission is granted, `canView()` returns `true` and `canView(client)` immediately returns `true` without evaluating permissions on the specific client's resource. Any negative/deny `view` permission configured for that specific client is therefore bypassed. `canView(ClientModel)` should check `canViewClientDefault()` (admin roles) rather than `canView()`, letting `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` handle the fallback to the all-clients resource when no client-specific resource exists.

findings.title: canView() does not return true when caller has manage permission on all clients
findings.body: `ClientPermissionsV2.canView()` only checks `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` and does not check `canManage()` (i.e. `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`). Because `canViewClientScopes()`, `requireViewClientScopes()`, `requireView()`, `canList()`, and `canListClientScopes()` in `ClientPermissions` all delegate to `canView()`, an administrator granted `manage` permission on all clients (without an explicit `view` scope or `query-clients` role) will have `canView()` return `false` and receive `403 Forbidden` on endpoints requiring view or list access to clients and client scopes.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission never finds individual client resources and returns resource type name
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` looks up client resources using `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates individual client resources without calling `resource.setType(resourceType)`, leaving their type as `null`. The only resource with type `"Clients"` is the all-clients resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init`, whose name is `"Clients"`. As a result, `getClientsWithPermission` never finds any individual client resources, and if the all-clients resource has the requested scope, it adds the literal string `"Clients"` instead of client IDs. In addition, `hasGrantedPermission` only checks `scope.equals(s)`, so `getClientsWithPermission("view")` will not include clients where the caller was granted `"manage"` or `"configure"`.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException and evaluation when adminPermissionsEnabled is disabled on the realm
findings.body: When `adminPermissionsEnabled` is turned off on a realm after the `admin-permissions` client has been initialized, `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient()` and `root.realmResourceServer()` remain non-null, while `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns `null` because `supportsAuthorizationSchema` checks `isAdminPermissionsEnabled(realm)`. In `hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, `resource` is not null-checked after calling `getResourceTypeResource`, so passing `null` to `findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()` will throw a `NullPointerException`. Furthermore, if a client-specific resource already exists (or in `hasPermission(String scope)` which queries `resourceStore.findByName` directly), permissions continue to be evaluated even though `adminPermissionsEnabled` is `false` on the realm.

findings.title: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName does not resolve Clients resources
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` only handles `USERS.getType()` and falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` for `CLIENTS.getType()`. Because `getOrCreateResource` creates client resources with `name = client.getId()` and does not set a `displayName`, calling `getResourceName` for a `Clients` policy (e.g. when querying a permission's resources via the Admin REST API) returns `null` for individual client resources instead of `client.getClientId()`, and `"Clients"` instead of `"All clients"` for the all-clients resource.
